results.note: Unlabelled app framing; no confidence claim. Crossing and rubbing are both named by Kansas City Rose Society and Texas A&M.

Portland 'back to the bud union, or back to the major cane'; Martin 'flush with the bud union or flush with the cane'. Disagreement shown: Kansas City 'back to the next outward facing bud'. Stands alone now.

ARS 'avoid the growth from being directed inward'; Texas A&M 'buds that point to the outside'; Victoria 'eye that is facing outwards'; Maryland 'grow outwards, not into the center'; Yates 'just above an outward-facing bud'. Centre-open phrase removed.

Prabhu 'graft union or a few inches above'; Victoria 'if above the graft - basal shoot'. Limit matches Eastcroft 'any part of it's stem above the union'. Make sure the limit field shows its own Low label.

Harkness 'often smaller, lighter in colour, or with more leaflets'; RHS 'different number of leaflets'; Treloar 'often notice' flowers differ; Eastcroft 'often more vigorous'; David Austin 'not always reliable'.

Content right and disagreement now stated (pull/tear side about 8 pages, cut side 4-5; RHS 'dormant basal buds are removed'; UCCE 'prevent the sucker from growing back'). Because the statement says sources disagree, it should carry 'Sources disagree' in place of Moderate (rules s3A).

Cut side: UCCE Ventura, Treloar, Fine Gardening ('cutting above...sprout faster'). Pull side: RHS FAQ ('don't just cut it off at soil level'), Harkness ('Cutting suckers at the surface encourages regrowth'). Both sides do say not at soil level.

package_notes: Only open point: removal_method[1] label. Use 'Sources disagree' instead of Moderate, or remove the disagreement sentence from it and leave that to removal_method[2].
